item.title: 50,000 Fake Stats Went Live, Google Forgot Them, ChatGPT Kept Citing Them — 7 Months Later I Read the Receipt
item.description: A public experiment from peec.ai: a brand-new domain generated 50,000 invented statistics with GPT-4.1 in a single day, for roughly $50 in total. Seven months on, Google deindexed it but ChatGPT never stopped pulling from it — 330+ referring domains, and the fake numbers ended up in an academic paper and a bank's investment research. I tear the citation-laundering chain apart and explain why sourcing every number is the one control that actually stops it.

item.title: dsh's Composer Started Guessing What You'll Say: 512 Tokens Buys Your Opening Move
item.description: DeepSeek Harness's community plugins give the dsh composer a 'guess what you'll say' layer: after each agent turn, ghost text drafts your next prompt and Tab adopts it. Bounded 512-token LLM calls plus local zsh-style prefix completion, with redaction and no core changes.

item.title: Exa 3.0 Tops Eight Benchmarks: The Number to Actually Watch Is the 0.3 Margin
item.description: Exa shipped 3.0 on 10-19: first place on all eight self-reported benchmarks, but the BrowseComp lead over Perplexity is 0.3 points. What actually changes the cost curve is Dynamic Highlights (95% fewer context tokens) plus Exa Lite at $4/1000 requests; independent scoring puts Exa at 80, tied for first.
